clue.text: Insight shown by hospital department, originally

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for department
first letter of hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital department shows sudden insight, at least at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth is profundity of understanding, so insight into something is a synonym.

clue.text: Business centre in Bangor, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: the commercial heart of a city
second meaning: Bangor is a town in County Down, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Looking for the commercial district of Bangor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DOWN TOWN: Bangor is a town in County Down in Northern Ireland, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtown is the usual word, especially in America, for a city's central commercial district.

clue.text: Old writer, popular within fold

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside another piece

blocks.note: a ply is a layer or fold, as in three-ply
what is in is fashionable and popular

explanation.surface: An ancient author is well liked among the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' here is a layer, not a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliny the Elder and Pliny the Younger were Roman authors, so either is an old writer.

clue.text: Struck senior teacher - row's made the papers

blocks.note: struck is the past tense of hit
the head is the senior teacher at a school
a row is a line, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A school scandal: a head teacher was struck and the fight was reported in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: HIT THE HEADLINES: the 's of row's supplies the final S rather than showing possession.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the headlines is an idiom for becoming front-page news, which is making the papers.

clue.text: Established practice in art? I do it differently with end of crayon

indicators.note: doing something differently means arranging it another way, so the letters are reordered
end of takes just the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
last letter of crayon

explanation.surface: An artist asks whether working with a crayon breaks with convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom long handed down, an established way of doing things.

clue.text: Bad time over in platoon?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over suggests turning the letters upside down so they read the other way

blocks.note: poor means bad, of low quality
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A soldier's unhappy spell of service is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: a troop is a unit of soldiers, like a platoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a small military unit, comparable in size to a platoon of infantry.

clue.text: One who might have excited NASA tutor?

definitions.text: One who might have excited NASA tutor?

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Who would thrill a space-agency instructor? A star pupil from orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: someone trained by NASA who might well have thrilled a tutor there.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a space traveller, trained by an agency such as NASA.

clue.text: Drink - two words for it!

blocks.note: first meaning: a fortified wine drunk as an aperitif
second meaning: the word it is short for these two words, as in gin and it

explanation.walkthrough: IT in 'gin and it' is short for ITALIAN VERMOUTH, so the clue's own word 'it' is spelt out in two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian vermouth is a sweet fortified wine, a drink mixed with gin in a classic cocktail.

clue.text: Lack of awareness in church sheltering good girl

indicators.note: sheltering means protecting something inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England
G is the abbreviation for good
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is unaware that a church is giving refuge to a well-behaved girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the wordplay: 'in church' is read whole, and the good girl goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is not knowing, a want of knowledge or awareness.

clue.text: Stockings, new, only ruined by son

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the word is broken up and its letters rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Brand-new stockings, the only pair, laddered by a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings made of the synthetic fibre nylon.

clue.text: American's vest in desert, reportedly shown on film

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by others, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a desert is a waste, which sounds like the part of the body
a film is a thin layer or coat

explanation.surface: An American's vest appears in a desert scene in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' is not a movie but a thin covering. Americans call a waistcoat a vest, while in Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment Americans call a vest is the sleeveless jacket the British call a waistcoat.

clue.text: Cancel yearbook missing second article

indicators.note: missing means left out, and second says which of two matching letters goes

blocks.note: an annual is a book published once a year
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone cancels the yearbook because the second article is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNUAL has two As; dropping the second leaves ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, as a marriage or contract is cancelled.

clue.text: Hamleys, say, developed photos - first of yours displayed inside

indicators.note: photographs are developed, but here developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
first of takes only the opening letter of the next word
displayed inside means put on show within something else

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of yours

explanation.surface: Your developed photos are on display in Hamleys.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamleys is a famous toy store on Regent Street in London; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamleys is an example of a store selling toys, a large and famous one.

clue.text: A rounded character, but not initially amusing man

indicators.note: not initially means without its first letter, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: comic means funny, amusing
a man's name

explanation.surface: A well-rounded personality who, at first, is no funny guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a letter of the alphabet, not a person: omicron is the Greek O, a round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the Greek letter O, a letter shaped like a circle.

clue.text: Women's crew, showering after end of work-out improving muscle performance

definitions.note: a gerund phrase standing for the activity, a noun

indicators.note: end of takes only the last letter of the following word
after places one piece behind another in the reading order

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a rowing crew of eight is called an eight
last letter of work-out
showering, of weather, is raining

explanation.surface: A women's rowing crew shower after their gym session, building up strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' is a rowing boat's eight, and 'showering' is the weather, not the changing room.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight training is exercise with weights, done to build strength and muscle.

clue.text: One bishop, one on board, is cranky

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
I is the Roman numeral one
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A bishop serving on a company board is grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a director; in a down clue 'on' just puts the second one above TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and cranky are synonyms, both meaning easily annoyed or bad-tempered.

clue.text: That rider is shaky, not much good

indicators.note: shaky means unsteady, so the letters wobble out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: That jockey is unsteady in the saddle and no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means inferior or of poor quality, so it is hardly any good.

clue.text: I'm mated, being handicapped

blocks.note: taken as written
mated means paired, as animals are

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that marriage holds them back.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means weakened or damaged in function, so hampered or handicapped.

clue.text: Fat American woman shown up by car headlight?

blocks.note: broad is American slang for a woman
something lit by a headlight is caught in its beam

explanation.surface: A large American woman is caught in a car's headlights.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is nautical: a broad-beamed ship is wide, so a person broad in the beam has wide hips.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad in the beam is an idiom for wide-hipped or stout, a polite way of saying fat.

clue.text: Criminal does, pocketing copper coin in use before the euro

definitions.text: coin in use before the euro

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, so the letters are bent out of order
pocketing means putting something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A crook pockets a copper coin from before the single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like part of the coin, but it is the chemical symbol. The escudo was Portugal's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the Portuguese currency until the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Resolved to live permanently with daughter

blocks.note: to settle is to make a permanent home
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone decides to move in for good with their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved to' reads as a decision, but 'Resolved' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled matter is one decided or sorted out, so resolved.

clue.text: Girl in cold area round a factory

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so letters sit on either side of another piece

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written
a mill is a factory

explanation.surface: A girl stands in a chilly yard around a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: After C, the A for area and the word a go round MILL, one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Camilla is a female given name, and a girl's name stands for a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: Thoroughly defeated a northern European, breaking record

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so pieces go within another

blocks.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian athlete wins easily and breaks a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking record' sounds like a sporting feat; here the letters break into CD.
explanation.definitionFit: To cane an opponent is informal for beating them heavily, a thorough defeat.

clue.text: Stand-in doctor reduced swelling across one's chest, initially

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its last letter
initially means at the start, so only the first letters of the words are taken
across means stretched over, so one piece spans either side of another

blocks.note: a lump is a swelling
first letters of one's and chest

explanation.surface: A substitute doctor shrinks a lump on a patient's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand-in doctor' is the definition, and 'reduced' sounds like treatment but trims LUMP to LUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor who temporarily stands in for another, a medical substitute.

clue.text: Living in a city, some favour banking

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part of the following words

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of favour and the start of banking

explanation.surface: City dwellers like a career in finance.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban means relating to towns and cities, so it describes city living.

clue.text: Can one run broadcast?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a single person can run a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as definition: the presenter is the one who can run a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer is the person who introduces programmes and reads links on radio or television.

clue.text: To exceed one's budget unfortunately proves point

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
a point is an end, as the point of a stick

explanation.surface: Going over budget, sadly, makes the case.
explanation.definitionFit: To overspend is to spend more than is available, which is exceeding a budget.

clue.text: Unpleasant odour I start to detect in damp

indicators.note: start to points to the beginning of the next word, so its first letter is kept

blocks.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
taken as written
first letter of detect

explanation.surface: Someone first notices a nasty smell in a damp room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' as a stench is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Humid describes air heavy with moisture, so muggy and damp.
